channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Young parliamentarians convene for global conference in Samarkand
item.description: The XII Global Conference of Young Parliamentarians, organized by the Senate of Uzbekistan and the Inter-Parliamentary Union, has begun in Samarkand. Approximately 250 delegates from 58 countries and 11 international organizations are attending the forum themed 'Towards restoring human rights, justice, and human dignity in challenging times'.

item.title: Escrow accounts facilitate over 33,000 property and vehicle deals in Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzbekistan's use of escrow accounts for real estate and vehicle transactions is expanding, ensuring secure and transparent settlements. In August 2026, 33,392 deals were completed using this mechanism, with Tashkent leading in transactions. This indicates growing trust in the system and sustained economic activity.

item.title: Uzbekistan implements new strategy to combat poverty and boost incomes
item.description: Uzbekistan has held a video conference to discuss measures for poverty reduction and income growth. The strategy focuses on new mechanisms at the mahalla, family, and individual levels. Poverty has decreased from 5.8% to a lower level, with 49 districts now free of unemployment and poverty, though some areas require further attention.

item.title: Car Accident in Dangara District Results in Pedestrian Fatality
item.description: A fatal road accident occurred in Dangara district on September 2, 2026, around 02:00. A Shacman truck driven by R. Rahmonov struck and killed pedestrian M. Ashurov. The Ministry of Internal Affairs of Tajikistan reported the incident, and an investigation is ongoing.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Over 71.9 Billion Soums of Gas and Electricity Embezzled in August
item.description: Uzbekistan's "Uzenergoinspeksiya" identified 321 cases of illegal energy resource use in August, totaling 71.9 billion soums. The inspections covered gas and electricity consumption across the country during the month.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Mandates Liability Insurance for Tour Operators
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet of Ministers has approved new rules requiring tour operators to provide tourists with medical or accident insurance. Liability limits will vary by route difficulty, with costs estimated at 400-500 soms per tourist per day. The resolution aims to increase tour package costs by only 1-2 percent and takes effect in ten days.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Ministry Staff Assist Over 40 People with Disabilities at World Nomad Games
item.description: Approximately 100 staff from Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Labor, Social Security, and Migration provided assistance to over 40 individuals with disabilities during the VI World Nomad Games. Special transport was arranged, and staff offered guidance and support to ensure accessibility for both local and foreign participants.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Considers Selling State Service Cars Directly to Employees
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering a proposal to allow government agencies to sell official vehicles directly to their employees before public auctions. The cars would be sold at market value to employees on a waiting list, potentially speeding up fleet renewal without additional state budget costs.

item.title: Tajikistan aims for "A" status for its Ombudsman institution
item.description: Tajikistan's Deputy Human Rights Ombudsman met with a UN regional advisor to discuss strengthening the institution's legal framework and human rights protection. The Ombudsman's office, currently holding "B" status since 2012, aims to achieve "A" status, which signifies full compliance with international standards for national human rights institutions.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan approves concept for science development until 2040
item.description: The Cabinet of Ministers of Kyrgyzstan has approved a concept for the development of science until 2040. This document outlines long-term directions for state policy in the field of science and aims to further develop research, higher education, intellectual property, and innovation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to revise cooperation approach with international organizations
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet of Ministers approved a new procedure for government agencies' cooperation with international bodies. This aims to improve effectiveness and clarify responsibilities. The Foreign Ministry will update the list of organizations and analyze cooperation results annually.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan mandates tour operators to insure tourists
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet of Ministers has approved rules requiring tour operators to provide mandatory insurance for tourists. This covers medical or accident insurance, with liability limits varying based on tour complexity: 3 million soms for standard tours and 5 million soms for extreme tours.

item.title: Tajikistan plans to develop GBAO energy system using digital technologies
item.description: Tajikistan's Deputy Minister of Energy and Water Resources, Parviz Yakhyezoda, met with the leadership of Pamir Energy to discuss the digitalization of the Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region's energy sector. The meeting focused on implementing modern digital technologies and expanding the digital economy's capabilities.

item.title: Netanyahu: Iranian Regime Will Soon Collapse Amid US Strikes
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu stated that the Iranian regime is struggling to maintain its existence following US attacks. He asserted that Tehran strikes neighboring countries out of fear of Israel's power, rather than directly attacking Israel.

item.title: Electric Train Service Launched Between Urgench Airport and Khiva
item.description: A new electric train service has commenced operations between Urgench Airport and Khiva in the Khorezm region. The train, manufactured by China's CRRC Dalian, can carry 415 passengers and reach speeds of up to 160 km/h. Tickets cost 25,000 UZS for adults.

item.title: American Climber Dies After Falling While Ascending Tajikistan's Ismoil Somoni Peak
item.description: Matt Dawson, a 47-year-old American climber, died after falling approximately 70-80 meters at an altitude of 5800 meters while attempting to summit Ismoil Somoni Peak in Tajikistan. The incident occurred on August 15, and his body was recovered on August 17.

item.title: Three Suspects Arrested for Drug Trafficking in Fergana and Namangan
item.description: Three individuals were apprehended in Fergana and Namangan regions for selling narcotics. Authorities discovered hashish and potent prescription drugs in their possession. Criminal cases have been initiated, and investigations are ongoing.

item.title: Uzbekistan Presented at CIGRE 2026; NURA Group Supports Global Energy Engagement
item.description: Uzbekistan was represented at CIGRE 2026, with NURA Group backing the nation's participation in the global energy community. This event highlights Uzbekistan's growing role and engagement in international energy discussions and collaborations.

item.title: US Vice President: China Ready to Help Isolate Iran, Cooperate on Sanctions
item.description: US Vice President Jey Di Vens stated that China is prepared to assist in isolating Iran and cooperate with Washington's plans for economic pressure. He also noted that oil shipments have returned to normal as Tehran lost control in the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan allocates 200 million soms for groundwater control and flood prevention
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is developing a project to manage drainage systems to reduce groundwater levels and prevent flooding and soil salinization. The Ministry of Emergency Situations will oversee operations. 200 million soms have already been allocated from the Stabilization Fund for these works, which include construction and repair of drainage systems.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan plans unified state registry for glaciers and enhanced protection measures
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is preparing amendments to its law on hydrometeorological activities to establish a unified state registry of glacier data and improve monitoring. The initiative aims to create a systematic state policy for protecting glaciers from pollution and reduction, including research and measures to slow degradation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan could attract 20-30 million tourists annually, says tourism agency head
item.description: Following major events like the World Nomad Games and SCO summits, Kyrgyzstan's tourism interest has surged globally. Eduard Kubatov, head of the State Tourism Agency, predicts tourist numbers could reach 20-30 million annually within years. He urges citizens to prepare accommodations, including yurts, to host visitors.

item.title: Uzbekistan Launches New Projects Ahead of Independence Day
item.description: Uzbekistan has launched 72 industrial and service projects and 91 social sphere facilities, totaling nearly 50 trillion Uzbekistani soums. These initiatives are expected to create 15,000 jobs and generate an additional 1 trillion soums in annual budget revenue. The economy has grown 2.5 times in the past decade, attracting $160 billion in foreign investment and launching 2,163 major industrial projects.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ready to Strengthen Comprehensive Strategic Partnership with China
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated that relations with China are at an unprecedentedly high level. Astana is prepared to consistently strengthen the eternal comprehensive strategic partnership with Beijing, enriching it with new content and opening new horizons for cooperation. He emphasized that the strong bilateral ties serve the fundamental interests of both nations and contribute to regional peace and stability.

item.title: Uzbekistan Delegation Attends Belgrade Summit on Non-Aligned Movement's 65th Anniversary
item.description: Uzbekistan's delegation, led by Sodik Safoev, participated in a high-level meeting in Belgrade commemorating the 65th anniversary of the Non-Aligned Movement. Safoev discussed the movement's current significance and Uzbekistan's preparation to chair it from 2027-2030, highlighting priorities like peace, security, economy, climate change, and youth issues.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Exports to Hong Kong Surge 22-Fold to $716 Million
item.description: Uzbekistan's exports to Hong Kong reached nearly $716 million in January-July, a 22-fold increase from $32.5 million in the same period last year, according to the National Statistics Committee. This surge has positioned Hong Kong as Uzbekistan's sixth-largest export market, surpassing Turkey and Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: New Book Explores Uzbekistan's Transformation Through the Lens of Its Women
item.description: A new book by Egyptian scholars Dr. Nabila Kandil and Dr. Ahmed Al-Zubaidi examines Uzbekistan's transformation under the 'New Uzbekistan' concept, focusing on the role of women. Published by Dar Al-Mustakbal Al-Arabi, it analyzes national changes through the lives of Uzbek women.

item.title: Muxsinxo‘ja Abdurahmonov Appointed Head of Migration Agency
item.description: Muxsinxo‘ja Abdurahmonov has been appointed the new director of the Migration Agency under the Cabinet of Ministers. He previously served as Uzbekistan's Ambassador to Japan since July 2021. Abdurahmonov holds degrees from Tashkent Economic University and has pursued further studies in Japan and the United States. He also has experience in the private sector and as a deputy governor.

item.title: Behzod Musayev Replaced as Head of Migration Agency
item.description: Behzod Musayev has been dismissed from his post as director of the Migration Agency. Muhsinxo‘ja Abdurahmonov, formerly Uzbekistan's Ambassador to Japan, has been appointed as his successor. The decision was signed by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Expects 20-30 Million Tourists Annually After Major Events
item.description: Kyrgyzstan anticipates a significant increase in tourism, potentially reaching 20-30 million visitors annually, following the World Nomad Games and SCO summits. Head of the State Agency for Tourism Eduard Kubatov stated that international media coverage has boosted interest in Kyrgyzstan. He urged citizens to prepare for hosting tourists, suggesting tourism could become a key economic driver for the country.

item.title: Uzbekistan to transform poverty reduction and income growth system
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev chaired a meeting on enhancing poverty reduction and income growth strategies. The poverty rate has decreased from 5.8% to 3.9%, with 1.5 million people now needing assistance. Despite significant resource allocation, regional effectiveness in poverty reduction varies.

item.title: Uzbek President's Aide Saida Mirziyoyeva Meets with Emir of Qatar in Doha
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of the Administration of the President of Uzbekistan, met with the Emir of Qatar, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, in Doha. They discussed strengthening bilateral relations and exploring new joint initiatives, noting significant potential for cooperation.

item.title: Iran considers Uzbekistan an important partner in Central Asia, says ambassador
item.description: Iran views Uzbekistan as a key partner in Central Asia, according to Iranian Ambassador Mukhammadali Iskandariy. He highlighted Uzbekistan's growing regional importance, driven by its economic, historical, and civilizational potential, and its foreign policy focused on good neighborliness and constructive dialogue.

item.title: Deputy suggests officials hindering democracy lack constitutional knowledge
item.description: Deputy Bobur Bekmurodov proposed that officials hindering democracy often lack sufficient knowledge of the Constitution. He suggested that state employees should be tested on their understanding of the Constitution.

item.title: German official praises Uzbekistan's reforms and future prospects
item.description: Johann Saathoff, Parliamentary State Secretary for Economic Cooperation and Development, stated that Uzbekistan's reforms in vocational education, public administration, and employment are creating a solid foundation for a bright future. He noted that these processes enhance the country's international authority and foster cooperation within Central Asia.

item.title: 1.2 km of Bus Rapid Transit lane opened on Shahrisabz Street in Tashkent.
item.description: A 1.2 km section of a Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) lane has been opened on Shahrisabz Street in Tashkent. The first phase of the project covers the area from the roundabout connecting Shahrisabz, Mirobod, and Shota Rustaveli streets to the intersection with Amir Temur Avenue.

item.title: Violations found in Kayyndy River water protection zone in Kyrgyzstan's Talas region.
item.description: Violations of land and water legislation were discovered in the village of Kayyndy, Talas region, Kyrgyzstan. The Ministry of Agriculture reported that light structures were built in the river's water protection zone, some close to the water. Soil cover was also damaged.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan plans to build a factory for producing vaccines against viruses and foot-and-mouth disease
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to construct a factory for producing biological preparations, including vaccines against viral and bacterial diseases, and foot-and-mouth disease. The project aims to strengthen the country's veterinary security and establish domestic vaccine production. Construction of veterinary laboratories is also being discussed.

item.title: Uzbek President discusses strengthening strategic partnership with US Senator
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev held discussions with a US Senator regarding further strengthening the strategic partnership between Uzbekistan and the United States. The parties also reviewed the development of inter-parliamentary cooperation.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva meets with the Emir of Qatar to discuss expanding relations.
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva met with the Emir of Qatar. During the meeting, they discussed expanding mutual relations and advancing new joint initiatives. Further details are available at the provided link.
